newsitem.title: INDIA: Inferno destroys New Delhi airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: Inferno destroys New Delhi airport terminal.

text.p: An early morning fire devastated the departure terminal for domestic Indian Airlines flights at New Delhi's airport on Wednesday but no casualties were reported or flights cancelled, airport officials said.
The blaze erupted at 0330 a.m. (2200 GMT Tuesday) and debris was still smouldering nine hours later.
An official in charge of airport operations, Robey Lal, said the fire broke out in the restaurant of the Indian Airlines terminal. The cause was not immediately known.
The whole structure of the terminal had crumbled and even the telephone booths and snacks kiosk were gutted.
"The fire was ferocious. It will take at least four months to reconstruct the terminal," Harbans Kumar, the airport director, told Reuters.
R.S. Tomar of Delhi Fire Service, one of the first to arrive at the scene, said: "I could see the red sky from almost a kilometre's distance and the flames were towering high up into the sky".
Kumar said the flames rose more than 30 feet (nine metres).
More than 50 fire-fighters in 10 vehicles reached the scene minutes after the blaze started, he added.
Tomar said if the fire had not been contained in time adjacent terminals could have caught fire.
"I thought some plane had caught fire," said Suresh Kumar a local resident and and eyewitness.
"The whole area was cordoned off by the police and fire fighters were pressing with the job for almost two hours before things came under control," said Dharamvir Kumar, another resident.
By mid-morning, soot covered much of the remains of the single-storey building built on New Delhi's outskirts in 1982.
Flight services were disrupted for three hours but resumed later from an adjacent terminal for private domestic airlines, officials said.

The airport's international terminal is in the same large area as the domestic terminals and was not affected by the fire, although airport officials said 10 international flights were diverted in the morning.
Indian civil aviation minister C.M. Ibrahim said a special committee will be set up to probe into the accident.
The terminal, for all flights operated by state-owned Indian Airlines, handled more than 20,000 passengers daily.
Air-India is the country's international airline.
